---
title: "Set up"
subtitle: "Colab takes two minutes and needs no install. JupyterLab on your laptop takes about 15 minutes, and uses all your cores."
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Which one?

**Colab** runs in your browser, so there's nothing to install. Its free tier gives you 2 cores. **JupyterLab on your
laptop** uses your own cores, often 8 or more. Both run the same notebook. Not sure? Start with Colab
([part A](#colab)). You can switch later.
:::

## A. Google Colab: nothing to install {#colab}

1. Open the [learner notebook in Colab]({{< var colab.learner >}}). The
   [filled notebook]({{< var colab.filled >}}) has every answer.
2. Sign in with your Google account.
3. Click **Copy to Drive** in the toolbar. Work in the new tab, titled
   **Copy of parallelization-with-python.ipynb**.
4. Click the first code cell under **Setup**, and press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}}. Run the next cell the same way.

**It works when** the first cell prints `downloaded fire.py` and `downloaded lanes.py`, and the second prints your
Python version and `start method: fork`.

A "not authored by Google" warning means you're in the original tab. Switch to your copy.

## B. JupyterLab on your laptop {#jupyterlab}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Did our Introduction to Programming with Python setup?

You already have uv and a `dss-python` folder with JupyterLab. Open a terminal, run `cd dss-python`, and skip to
[step 6](#notebook).
:::

### 1. Open a terminal

A terminal is a window where you type commands instead of clicking.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Mac

Press {{< kbd Cmd-Space >}}, type **Terminal**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

#### Windows

Press the {{< kbd Win >}} key, type **PowerShell**, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}. Your prompt starts with `PS C:\`.
:::

### 2. Install uv

uv is one small tool that installs Python and the packages you need. It needs no admin rights. Copy the line for your
computer, paste it into the terminal, and press {{< kbd Enter >}}.

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Mac

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```
:::

#### Windows (PowerShell)

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
```
:::
:::

### 3. Check it worked

**Close the terminal and open a new one**, so it can find uv. Then run:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv --version
```
:::

You should see a version number.

### 4. Make your project folder

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv init --python {{< var python >}} --vcs none --no-package dss-parallel
cd dss-parallel
```
:::

The folder is made in your home folder. `--python {{< var python >}}` matches the Python that Colab uses, so the
notebook behaves the same in both places.

### 5. Add JupyterLab, matplotlib and psutil

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv add jupyterlab matplotlib psutil
```
:::

**This is the slow step.** It's done when your prompt comes back. Download the notebook (step 6) while you wait.

### 6. Download the notebook {#notebook}

- [Download the learner notebook]({{< var download.learner >}}){download="" data-noresolveinput=""}: blank code to
  write with us. This is the one you need.
- [Download the filled notebook]({{< var download.filled >}}){download="" data-noresolveinput=""}: every answer, to
  check your work.

Your browser saves them in your Downloads folder.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Prefer the terminal?

Run this inside your project folder. The notebook lands right there, so you can skip dragging it in (step 7).

::: {.panel-tabset}
#### Mac

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
curl -LO {{< var raw.learner >}}
```
:::

#### Windows (PowerShell)

Type `curl.exe`, with the `.exe`. Plain `curl` in PowerShell is a different tool.

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```powershell
curl.exe -LO {{< var raw.learner >}}
```
:::
:::
:::

### 7. Start JupyterLab and run the Setup cells

Once step 5 is finished, run this in your project folder:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
uv run jupyter lab
```
:::

Your browser opens JupyterLab. **Leave the terminal open.** It's running JupyterLab.

1. Drag the notebook from your Downloads folder onto JupyterLab's file list in the left sidebar. Or click the
   **Upload** button (↑) above the file list, and choose the file.
2. Double-click the notebook to open it.
3. Click the first code cell under **Setup**, and press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}}. Run the next cell the same way.

**It works when** the first cell prints `downloaded fire.py` and `downloaded lanes.py` (it needs the internet this
once), and the second prints your Python version and `start method: spawn` on a Mac or Windows.

### 8. Stop, and start again later

Save your work with {{< kbd mac=Cmd-S win=Ctrl-S >}}. To stop JupyterLab, go back to the terminal and press
{{< kbd Ctrl-C >}} twice. Next time, open a terminal and run:

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
cd dss-parallel
uv run jupyter lab
```
:::

### Already use conda?

Use these commands instead of steps 2 to 5, in Terminal on a Mac, or in Anaconda Prompt or Miniforge Prompt on
Windows. Then continue with step 6, and skip the `uv run jupyter lab` command: the last line starts JupyterLab.

::: {.prompt .prompt-shell}
```bash
conda create -y -n dss-parallel -c conda-forge --override-channels python={{< var python >}} jupyterlab matplotlib psutil
conda activate dss-parallel
mkdir dss-parallel
cd dss-parallel
jupyter lab
```
:::

The first command is one long line. Use the copy button.

## If something goes wrong

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `uv: command not found` | Open a new terminal. Still missing on a Mac? Run `source $HOME/.local/bin/env`. |
| "running scripts is disabled" (Windows) | Use the exact command in step 2, with `-ExecutionPolicy ByPass`. |
| The browser didn't open | Copy the `http://localhost:…` link from the terminal and paste it into your browser. |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fire'` | Run the first Setup cell. It downloads `fire.py` and `lanes.py` next to the notebook. |
| `HTTPError` or `URLError` in the first cell | The download was blocked. Save [fire.py](notebooks/fire.py){download="" data-noresolveinput=""} and [lanes.py](notebooks/lanes.py){download="" data-noresolveinput=""} into the notebook's folder. |
| `Can't get attribute 'work' on <module '__main__'>` | Your worker function is defined in a cell. Put it in a `.py` file, as the template does with `%%writefile`. |
| A cell runs forever | Stop it (■), then restart: **Kernel → Restart Kernel** in JupyterLab, **Runtime → Restart session** in Colab. Run the cells again from the top. |
| Chromebook or tablet | Use Colab ([part A](#colab)). |

<p class="small-muted">uv changes often. If a screen looks different, the
<a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/">official install page</a> wins. Help with your own
setup: <a href="{{< var help >}}">go.ncsu.edu/getdatahelp</a>.</p>
